对话 1 欢迎收看我们的节目，朋友们，关系。
Conversation 1 Welcome to our programme, Friends and Relationships.
我们今天的嘉宾是来自麦吉尔大学。
Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.
很高兴来到这里，简。
Glad to be here, Jane.
你好，史蒂夫。
Hi, Steve.
我们今天的问题是为什么朋友突然消失？
Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear?
他们可能会在社交媒体上屏蔽我们帐户并停止回复我们的电子邮件。
They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails.
他们就消失得无影无踪了。
They simply vanish without a trace.
依恋风格？
Attachment styles?
当与他们的父母，患有焦虑型依恋的孩子尖叫并哭着叫父母过来后退。
When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back.
但其他孩子只是关闭并尝试通过忽略来处理他们的情绪情况。
But other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation.
这些依恋风格会延续到成年。
And these attachment styles carry on into adulthood.
逃避能减轻他们的压力水平吗？
Does avoidance reduce their stress levels?
并不真地。
Not really.
他们的压力水平实际上和那些大喊大叫的孩子所经历的尖叫。
Their stress levels are actually the same as those experienced by the children who yell and scream.
我认为，这两者都可以称为不安全的。
And I assume both might be termed insecure.
确切地。
Exactly.
这是一种非常不安全的依恋。
And it's a very insecure attachment.
和冲突是一样的。
It's the same as conflicts.
因此，如果你与安全依恋的人，他们不会恐慌。
So if you have a disagreement with a securely attached person, they're not going to panic.
他们能够听到对方说的话表达自己的感受和有效地思考。
They're able to hear what the other person is saying and express their own feelings and thoughts effectively.
然而，缺乏安全感的人则不会。
However, an insecurely attached person won't.
它们可能会攻击你、防御你或者从你的生活中消失。
They might either attack you, get defensive or just disappear from your life.
对他们来说，无论差异有多小，在你的眼中，标志着关系。
To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.
这也解释了它们为何突然消失。
That explains why they suddenly disappear.
对话 2。
Conversation 2.
听说你很快就要去日本了。
I hear you're going to Japan soon.
是的，没错。
Yes, that's right.
我能请你帮个忙吗？
Could I ask you a favour?
当然。
Sure.
它是什么？
What is it?
我想知道你能否帮我当你在那里时，可以买一些牛仔裤。
I was wondering if you could get me some jeans while you're there.
我当然会还给你。
I'll pay you back, of course.
一条牛仔裤？
A pair of jeans?
好的。
Okay.
我不明白为什么不行。
I don't see why not.
但这里的牛仔裤有什么问题呢？
But what's wrong with jeans here?
嗯，我只是喜欢好的牛仔裤和日本恰巧做到了世界上最好的。
Well, I just love good jeans and Japan happens to make the best in the world.
我的朋友从那里给我买了一双五年前就已经使用了，但它们看起来仍然很新。
My friend brought me a pair from there five years ago and they still look new.
真的吗？
Really?
我不知道日本生产牛仔裤。
I had no idea Japan made jeans.
我本以为美国做得最好牛仔裤，因为它是典型的美国服装。
I would have thought America made the best jeans because it's a typical American garment.
是的，我也这么认为。
Yeah, I thought so too.
但事实证明日本仍然有一些拥有传统编织工具的古老磨坊用于以原始方式制作牛仔裤。
But it turns out Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools used to make jeans the original way.
制作衣服的过程比较慢，但是最终结果肯定是更优异的。
It's a slower process of making clothing but the end result is surely superior.
此外，他们使用的面料是品质更高，染料也是天然的。
Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural.
它们的编织更紧密，而且更比世界上任何其他牛仔裤都耐用。
They have a denser weave and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.
听起来很酷。
That sounds cool.
我的腰围是 34，尺码是 30或长度为32。
I have a 34 waist and size 30 or 32 in length.
都可以。
Either is fine.
它们的价格应该在 500 美元左右，但利润却翻了一番确信它们是日本制造的。
They should be around $500 but make double certain they are made in Japan.
500美元？
$500?
天哪，这太贵了。
Boy, that's expensive.
你通常会花那么多钱买一条休闲裤？
Do you typically spend that much on a pair of casual trousers?
是的，它们有点贵，但是它们非常特别。
They are a little pricey, yes, but they are very special.
请记住它们可以持续我好几年年，而且它们也非常时尚。
Bear in mind they will last me several years and they are very fashionable too.
我认为它们绝对值得。
I think they're totally worth it.
